subject: Re: Confirmation of model-improvement prohibition and subprocessor evidence request
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@novamed.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Novamed Legal <legal@novamed.com>; Priya Shah <priya.shah@novamed.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T09:12:00Z
Subject: Model-improvement prohibition + evidence request

Hannah —

Thanks for the demo earlier. As we start procurement, our legal and security teams have two high-level asks that we need to see supported before we proceed:

1) Contractual commitment: an explicit prohibition on using any Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or improve Redwood models (including any downstream internal training pipelines). We typically call this a "training ban" clause; flagged language is attached to the DPA redline.

2) Operational evidence: we need verifiable evidence of existing controls and subprocessors for residency and handling (EU-only storage preference, list of subprocessors with country of processing, and a remediation plan if any subprocessor processes data outside agreed regions). Specifically: KMS residency options (onshore KMS or HSM integration), SFTP or API export path for custody, and a sample ops-evidence pack (screenshots, attestations, brief runbook).

Additionally, our product team has questions about ownership of prompts and LLM outputs: we need confirmation that prompt/response artifacts submitted by users remain customer-owned and not used to create derivative rights for Redwood.

I've attached our DPA redline (Novamed_DPA_redline_v1.docx). Can you confirm what you can commit to and share an evidence timeline?

Appreciate a concise plan and timeline — we have an internal milestone to sign vendor agreements by 2026-11-25.

Regards,
Liam
Director, Platform Security
Novamed

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@novamed.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Novamed Legal <legal@novamed.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T14:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Model-improvement prohibition + evidence request

Hi Liam —

Thanks — and great to meet yesterday. We can and should be explicit about the commitments you need. High level summary of what Redwood can offer and proposed next steps:

- Contract language (proposal): "Redwood shall not use, access, or process Customer Content for the purpose of training, fine-tuning, or improving any models or model parameters. Where Redwood stores or processes Customer Content, it will do so only for the provision of the Services as defined in the Agreement." (Legal: see attached suggested redline).

- Prompt/response ownership: customer prompts and generated outputs will be treated as Customer Content. Redwood will not assert ownership over prompt/response artifacts and will not derive or license customer outputs for model improvement. We'll add explicit confidentiality tagging to the DPA.

- Subprocessors & residency: we will provide an up-to-date subprocessor roster with processing location per subprocessor and a short attestation for each location. For EU residency preference we support onshore routing where feasible and can expose KMS residency options (customer-managed KMS via Bring-Your-Own-Key or a contractually committed region-specific KMS).

- Evidence pack & timeline: David (cc'd) will produce an ops-evidence checklist and an initial pack (subprocessor list, KMS config screenshots, runbook excerpts) within 7 business days. Full ops-evidence pack (including SFTP transfer test and sample attestations) within 12 business days. We've attached an "ops-evidence-checklist.pdf" as the starting scope.

- Proposed MAP: we'll map milestones and deliverables into a short mutual action plan (MAP) and can route the DPA redline for a single consolidated signature via DocuSign once evidence milestones are agreed.

Next steps we propose:
1) Confirm the DPA redline you shared (we'll produce our redline with the training ban language tracked).
2) David to hand off ops-evidence pack within 7 business days.
3) We mutually agree the MAP and sign the DPA with the committed language.

Marissa will own the procurement cadence and can coordinate calendar availability for a 30-min legal sync if needed.

Attachments: suggested DPA redline, ops-evidence-checklist.pdf

Thanks — will follow up with the evidence pack.

Best,
Hannah
Head of Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@novamed.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@novamed.com>, Novamed Legal <legal@novamed.com>
Date: 2026-11-11T10:21:00Z
Subject: Re: Model-improvement prohibition + evidence request

Hannah —

Thanks for the clear response. A couple of clarifying questions from legal/security before we proceed:

- KMS/BYOK: when you say "customer-managed KMS via BYOK," can you confirm which cloud KMS providers and regions are supported for BYOK (we are asking EU-only keys for this engagement)? Is HSM integration (customer-owned HSM) possible for our dedicated instances?

- Derivative rights language: we need an explicit line that prevents Redwood from granting any third party rights to customer prompts/outputs (i.e., "no assignment or license of outputs to third parties without Customer consent"). Can you provide the exact wording you plan to include?

- Evidence granularity: we will need the ops-evidence pack to include at least one SFTP transfer test (proof of exportability), a KMS config export (screenshot + metadata), and a subprocessor locality attestation signed by Redwood operations. Will David be able to provide the SFTP test within the 12-business-day window?

Finally, please confirm retention windows you expect to apply to prompts and session logs (we will need options for 7, 30, and 90-day retention policies).

If you can land a short MAP with dates today, we can align Novamed's internal approval path.

Regards,
Priya Shah
Sr. Counsel, Novamed

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@novamed.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@novamed.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Novamed Legal <legal@novamed.com>
Date: 2026-11-11T15:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Model-improvement prohibition + evidence request — MAP and next steps

Priya / team —

Appreciate the precision. Below is a concise MAP and responses to your questions. If this looks good we'll convert the MAP into a shared spreadsheet and begin evidence delivery.

MAP (milestones & owners):
- 2026-11-11: Redwood to confirm proposed DPA clause language (below) and MAP milestones — OWNER: Hannah (done).
- 2026-11-18 (7 business days): Ops-evidence checklist deliverable v1 (subprocessor roster with locations, KMS configuration screenshots, runbook excerpts) — OWNER: David Kim.
- 2026-11-25 (12 business days): Full ops-evidence pack including SFTP transfer test logs, signed subprocessor locality attestations, and KMS export metadata — OWNER: David Kim.
- 2026-11-29: Parties execute DPA via DocuSign after confirmatory review — OWNER: Marissa Cole.

Responses / clarifications:
- BYOK & HSM: supported KMS providers for EU BYOK: AWS KMS (eu-west-1 / eu-central-1), GCP KMS (europe-west1), Azure Key Vault (West Europe). For dedicated/private deployments we support customer-owned HSMs (via VPN/IP allowlist and an HSM integration pattern) — this is routable for dedicated capacity and private installs; we'll provide the integration checklist in the ops pack.

- Proposed derivative/third-party wording (suggestion for the DPA): "Redwood shall not grant, assign, or license any rights to Customer Content, prompts, or outputs to any third party without Customer's prior written consent. Customer Content and derived artifacts shall remain Customer Confidential Information and Customer retains all ownership rights over such Content and outputs." (legal: happy to iterate).

- Evidence granularity & SFTP test: David confirms SFTP test will be included with sample logs and transfer verification artifacts in the 12-business-day pack. We will also include a short video walkthrough for the KMS export metadata if helpful.

- Retention windows: Redwood supports configurable retention windows at 7, 30, 90 days for prompts/session logs for Hosted and Dedicated. Default is 30 days; we can commit to 7/30/90-day options by configuration and document the chosen window in the DPA.

Attached: MAP spreadsheet (MAP-Novamed-Redwood.xlsx) and ops-evidence-checklist.pdf.

If Novamed confirms the MAP dates above, David will start the evidence run and Marissa will kick the DocuSign flow.

Thanks — we aim to keep this tight to meet your vendor sign-off timeline.

Best,
Hannah
Head of Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference
